tools.name: rank
tools.description: Legacy v1; use decide for new work. Which models rank highest for one fixed use-case profile? Returns a shortlist for that profile with evidence_basis, which is input provenance (none, unverified-legacy, mixed, partial-verified, verified), not a quality verdict. Needs an API key (Authorization: Bearer). Costs 1 credit a call; a credit costs $0.0017–$0.004 depending on the plan or pack (https://modelspec.dev/pricing/). Don't call it when you can state requirements: decide takes them, rank doesn't. Proxies POST https://api.modelspec.dev/v1/rank with this tool's arguments as the JSON body. Null means not researched or not published, never a guess. Every sourced value on a card carries a URL and a read date. This tool returns the origin's JSON plus the origin URL; it does not invent fields.

use_case.description: Ranking profile id, as published in /api/rank/profiles.json

x-meaning.local: on the caller's own machine; requires downloadable weights
x-meaning.managed_api: a provider or gateway API; no weights requirement
x-meaning.self_hosted: on infrastructure the caller runs; requires downloadable weights

tools.name: model_info
tools.description: What does ModelSpec's published card say about one model? Reads https://modelspec.dev/api/models/<model_id>.json (model_id is provider/slug). With data splitting enabled, returns only the model's display name from the Worker vocabulary. Free, no key. Not current evidence and not a ranking: use decide for that. Null means not researched or not published, never a guess. Every sourced value on a card carries a URL and a read date. This tool returns the origin's JSON plus the origin URL; it does not invent fields.

tools.name: list_use_cases
tools.description: Which ranking profiles exist, and what is the ranking policy? Returns https://modelspec.dev/api/rank/profiles.json: the profiles, the evidence floors and the neutrality commitment, as data. Free, no key. Not a decision: use decide for that. Null means not researched or not published, never a guess. Every sourced value on a card carries a URL and a read date. This tool returns the origin's JSON plus the origin URL; it does not invent fields.

tools.name: policy_check
tools.description: Which models, on which platforms, does my policy allow? Checks a policy document (licence, origin, data handling) per model and per platform. Returns pass, fail or undetermined for each row; undetermined is not a pass. Needs an API key (Authorization: Bearer). Costs 5 credits a call; a credit costs $0.0017–$0.004 depending on the plan or pack (https://modelspec.dev/pricing/). It doesn't choose a model: use decide to choose among the ones that pass. Proxies POST https://api.modelspec.dev/v1/policy-check with this tool's arguments as the JSON body; Authorization is forwarded. Null means not researched or not published, never a guess. Every sourced value on a card carries a URL and a read date. This tool returns the origin's JSON plus the origin URL; it does not invent fields.

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Which models fit this job? ModelSpec is an analysis of alternatives for AI models: it decides which models fit a job from your requirements, sourced benchmarks and real cost, and shows its work. Returns the answer (one model, or a declared tie that names the cheapest, open-weights and best-measured members), ranked results with cost per task and uncertainty, the models screened out with the reason for each, may_qualify for missing facts, and a decision_id and snapshot so the same spec gives the same answer later. Needs an API key (Authorization: Bearer). Costs 1 or 2 credits a call; a credit costs $0.0017–$0.004 depending on the plan or pack (https://modelspec.dev/pricing/). Not a router: call it once per job or role, not per request, then route among the models it recommends. Proxies POST https://api.modelspec.dev/v1/decide. Read vocab first with section=starter for valid facet ids. Put Musts in where: these gates exclude. Put Prefers in optimize.weights: weights rank and never exclude. Unknown values go to may_qualify instead of being dropped. Pin snapshot for reproducibility. Example for a coding agent on a budget: {"spec_version":1,"snapshot":"latest","capabilities":{"software_engineering":"required"},"where":["model.class = text-generator","model.context_window >= 200000","offering.cost_per_task <= 0.25"],"optimize":{"weights":{"software_engineering":0.6,"-offering.cost_per_task":0.4}}}. Use explain: "summary" (the default): 1 credit, and it carries the answer, results, by_model and may_qualify. explain: "full" (2 credits) also lists every eliminated candidate and returns about 670 KB, so ask for it only to see why one model was excluded. The decision response is returned unchanged with a short summary. Authorization from the MCP client is forwarded. Null means not researched or not published, never a guess. Every sourced value on a card carries a URL and a read date. This tool returns the origin's JSON plus the origin URL; it does not invent fields.

Soft.description: A soft condition: violating it costs ``penalty`` of the objective instead of eliminating.
Soft.title: Soft

Known.description: ``known(facet)``: passes when the facet is known. It is never unknown itself.
Known.title: Known

InSet.description: ``facet in {a, b}`` or ``facet not in {a, b}``. Values are kept sorted and unique.
InSet.title: InSet

EvidenceQualifiers.description: Which evidence may satisfy a condition on an evidence facet.
EvidenceQualifiers.title: EvidenceQualifiers

Compare.description:
``facet op value``; the value may be ``model(<id>)`` or ``best(m)`` for a relative
condition.
Compare.title: Compare

BestRef.description:
``facet >= best(m)``: within ``m`` of the highest value among the candidates
that pass every other hard condition. Added in 2.11.
BestRef.title: BestRef

ModelRef.description: The right-hand side of a relative condition: ``coding >= model(openai/gpt-6-sol)``.
ModelRef.title: ModelRef

TaskTokens.description: How many tokens one task takes. ``offering.cost_per_task`` is priced from it.
TaskTokens.title: TaskTokens

Preference.description: A weighted preference for one value of a boolean or enum facet.
Preference.title: Preference

Tolerance.description: How far below the best a lexicographic step may be and still tie: ``5%`` or a number.
Tolerance.title: Tolerance

Estate.description:
What the caller holds, sent with the spec and never stored. Added in 2.3.

``providers`` are provider IDs the caller has a key for, ``plans`` are
subscription plan IDs, ``devices`` are hardware SKU IDs. ``exhausted`` lists
providers or plans that cannot be used right now; an exhausted provider
takes its key and its plans with it.
Estate.title: Estate

Access.description:
How the caller will use the model. Added in 2.6.

``chat_app``: a provider's chat app, through a subscription plan.
``coding_tool``: a coding harness, through a plan or pay-per-use;
``harness`` names one from ``registry/harnesses.yaml`` (any when absent).
``own_software``: the caller's own software, pay-per-use (or a plan whose
surfaces include ``api``). ``own_hardware``: self-hosted on the caller's
devices. A spec may give the bare kind as a string.
Access.title: Access

tools.name: vocab
tools.description: What can a decide spec say? Returns the decision vocabulary: valid facet ids, benchmarks, domains, providers and task types. Compact by default, with 20 rows per page and no counts. In split mode full details still exclude per-model facts and counts. Free, no key. Call it before writing a spec, not to compare models. Call vocab section=starter first for the facets used most by the 40 template specs. Use search for a case-insensitive substring of id or label, then call decide. Pass id or ids for full details of specific rows, or detail=full for all display details. Use offset and limit to page compact sections; an empty page ends the list. Read vocab first with section=starter for valid facet ids. Put Musts in where: these gates exclude. Put Prefers in optimize.weights: weights rank and never exclude. Unknown values go to may_qualify instead of being dropped. Pin snapshot for reproducibility. Example for a coding agent on a budget: {"spec_version":1,"snapshot":"latest","capabilities":{"software_engineering":"required"},"where":["model.class = text-generator","model.context_window >= 200000","offering.cost_per_task <= 0.25"],"optimize":{"weights":{"software_engineering":0.6,"-offering.cost_per_task":0.4}}}.

section.description: Return only this vocabulary section; defaults to starter

search.description: Case-insensitive substring over id and label or display name

id.description: Return full details for this exact id

ids.description: Return full details for these exact ids

detail.description: Full returns all display details; defaults to compact

offset.description: Skip this many matching rows; defaults to 0

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Was a ModelSpec answer reliable? After you act on an answer, say whether it was reliable, unreliable, trustworthy, untrustworthy or confusing, by proxying POST https://api.modelspec.dev/v1/feedback. Include the answer's decision_id. Free, no key, and no Authorization header is forwarded. Not for questions or support. Never put a prompt, a key or personal details in note. The response says status "recorded" or "not_recorded" (storage is off until the privacy statement covers it).

input_schema.title: ModelSpec feedback
input_schema.description: POST this to https://api.modelspec.dev/v1/feedback. No key. One rating from a fixed set, optionally tied to the decision_id of a ModelSpec answer. Never include a prompt, a key, or anything that identifies a person. Reference: https://github.com/turbobeest/modelspec/blob/main/docs/feedback-api.md

rating.description: What you thought of the answer or the page.

decision_id.description: The decision_id of the answer this is about.

note.description: Optional. What was wrong or right, in your words.

trying_to_decide.description: Optional. What you were trying to decide.

template.description: Optional. The decision template in use.
